rationale: Both Gospels tell the same sequence in the same order: Jesus teaches from a boat to a crowd on the shore, tells the parable of the four soils, is asked about it privately, answers with words from Isaiah 6:9-10, and explains each soil. Checked in this app’s BSB, the parable itself is close to verbatim (“Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow,” Matthew 13:5 and Mark 4:5 alike). The differences are checkable: Mark’s yields run “thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold” (4:8) where Matthew’s run from a hundredfold down; Mark has “so that” (4:12, Greek hina) where Matthew has “This is why…” with a causal clause (13:13, Greek hoti); Mark ends the Isaiah words “and be forgiven” (4:12) where Matthew has “and I would heal them” (13:15); Mark names “Satan” (4:15) where Matthew has “the evil one” (13:19); and only Matthew has the blessing on the disciples’ eyes and ears (13:16-17). Graded parallel/strong, following conn-matt9-ruler-mark5: no citation links the two accounts, and the overlap is substantial while the differences are real. Which account depends on which is not decided by this connection.
